The combination of harbor masts, waterfront boulevard with curved lamp posts, and a green hill beside the road matches Hamburg’s St. Pauli Landungsbrücken area rather than other German port cities (e.g., Kiel/Bremen lack this exact configuration of promenade, hill “Stintfang,” and dense tourist traffic).

On the left is a grassy hill/park (Stintfang) that rises immediately above the Landungsbrücken, with billboard and stair/paths leading down—this arrangement is distinctive at the junction by Helgoländer Allee/Hafenstraße near the Landungsbrücken terminals. Flags on poles atop the buildings by the waterfront and the visible sailing-ship rigging align with the tourist piers. These elements together pinpoint the street segment approaching St. Pauli Landungsbrücken from the west (Helgoländer Allee/Hafenstraße).
